simulation.organization_and_actors: Medium or large Brazilian employer; employee-service desk, payroll/benefits operations, occupational-health administration, and HR case specialists.
processes: classify and route employee-service requests from short free-text descriptions
extract bounded administrative fields from absence and return-to-work requests before deterministic eSocial and policy validation
triage workplace-conduct or service-recovery narratives without deciding merit, discipline, health status, or employment outcome
simulation.baseline: Structured forms, mandatory fields, HR-service taxonomy, keyword and rules routing, eSocial validation rules, queues, RBAC, confidentiality controls, and specialist review.
simulation.remaining_gap: A compact classifier could reduce residual manual triage, but the capability is already available in HR service-delivery platforms and does not define a differentiated business outcome. Sensitive narratives also require abstention and human ownership.

training_data.observation_unit: One employee-service or administrative HR case at its initial triage point.
training_data.input_data: Initial short description, employee-selected service, channel, locale, organization context, and only fields available before routing.
training_data.target_or_reward: Human-confirmed HR service, routing destination, or bounded extracted administrative fields.
training_data.label_source: Final specialist correction and resolved service category; assumed available but quality and consistency are unknown.
training_data.prediction_time: Immediately after intake and before specialist reassignment, investigation, medical interpretation, or case resolution.
training_data.expected_volume: Unknown; must be measured per employer and service taxonomy.
training_data.class_balance: Unknown and likely long-tailed across common payroll/benefit requests and rare sensitive cases.
training_data.historical_coverage: Unknown; taxonomy changes, mergers, policy revisions, and channel differences may fragment history.
training_data.train_validation_split: Time-based split with organization/service-version isolation; no random split across duplicated or reopened cases.
training_data.leakage_risks: Final assignment, resolution notes, specialist identity, medical conclusions, disciplinary outcomes, and fields added after reassignment.
training_data.representativeness_risks: Language, literacy, disability, region, role, channel, union context, and organization-specific taxonomy differences.
training_data.feedback_loop: Specialist corrections can improve labels, but model-suggested categories may reinforce prior routing conventions.
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: Employment, health, grievance, conduct, and accommodation narratives require purpose limitation, access control, minimization, retention controls, and prohibition on autonomous employment decisions.
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: Use structured intake, rules, search, taxonomy maintenance, confidence abstention, and manual triage.

portfolio_comparison.reason: The candidate repeats bounded text classification, extraction, and routing already represented in the portfolio and commercially delivered by HR service-management platforms.

existing_landscape.overlap: ServiceNow HR Service Delivery Predictive Intelligence already auto-determines HR service from the case short description and supports HR case routing and specialist workspaces.

where_ai_enters.primary_mechanism: Compact text classification or bounded entity extraction for initial HR-case triage.
where_ai_enters.human_control: HR specialists retain routing correction, confidentiality handling, investigation, medical interpretation, grievance, discipline, accommodation, and employment decisions.
